classification.difficultyReason: Plot paired wind-speed and temperature values on labelled, scaled axes, then translate the downward pattern into a contextual statement of tendency.

content.prompt: The maximum wind speed and maximum temperature in a location were recorded for 2 weeks. The data is displayed in the table below.

inlines.text: Construct a scatterplot of the data given in the table.

spec.description: Blank square coordinate grid with arrowed axes, additional unnumbered ticks and labelled wind-speed and temperature axes.
spec.mathematics: Both axes range from 0 to 30; grid interval 2.5; numbered ticks at 5, 10, 15, 20, 25 and 30.
spec.answerVisibility: No data points in the question figure.

answer.worked: Use wind speed as $x$ and temperature as $y$. Plot one point for each paired column of the table, without joining the points.

spec.description: Complete scatterplot of all 14 paired observations.
spec.answerVisibility: Completed plot appears only in answers.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Are there any conclusions to be drawn from the scatterplot?

answer.short: As wind speed increases, temperature tends to decrease.
answer.worked: The points trend downwards from left to right. As wind speed increases, temperature tends to decrease.
